narrative.overview:
The Hub reads like a well-run research library: quiet rooms, clear shelving, and labels that tell you exactly where you are. Serif headings give each page the authority of a published protocol; a plain sans-serif body and generous line height keep long technical guidance easy to read for staff who use English as a second language. The mood is precise, technical, and efficient. Nothing on the page is decorative for its own sake; every color, border, and badge tells the reader something (what kind of page this is, what kind of note this is, what the main action is).

Density follows the Quarto docs layout: a section sidebar on the left, a single reading column in the middle, and a table of contents with authorship metadata in the right margin. Brand color is concentrated in a few confident places: the homepage hero band, the action buttons, the page-type badge, and the cookie notice. Everything else sits on paper white (light) or reading-room black (dark), and both themes are first-class.
keyCharacteristics: Serif headings (Gelasio bold), sans-serif body (Arimo), monospace only for code (Fira Code); all three self-hosted.
Color marks meaning: Diátaxis page type, callout kind, primary action, brand moment.
Soft-edged, confident components: pill buttons and badges, hairline-bordered callouts with a faint tint.
Flat pages; shadows only on layers that float above the page.
Light and dark themes share one token vocabulary (`--brand-*`, `--hub-*`).

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Color appears only where it carries meaning: page type, callout kind, primary action, or a brand moment (hero, cookie notice). Running text and surfaces stay neutral.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: Never hard-code a palette hex in CSS. Use `var(--brand-*)` for palette colors and `var(--hub-*)` for values that differ by theme; any remaining hex value needs a comment saying why.

rules.name: The Checked Pair Rule
rules.body: Every color pairing is checked in both themes: text at 4.5:1 or more, icons and focus rings at 3:1 or more. When a brand color fails, use a darker or lighter palette step (Meadow Green, Ember Orange), not a new color.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Gelasio is for headings, Arimo for everything a reader reads or clicks, Fira Code only for code. Never set body text, buttons, or labels in the serif, and never use monospace as decoration.

rules.name: The Reading Measure Rule
rules.body: Keep running text in the 900px body column (about 65--75 characters per line). Wide content (tables, code output) scrolls inside its own box instead of widening the column.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Anything that is part of the page is flat. Only elements that float over the page (menus, the cookie notice) cast a shadow.

rules.name: The No-Stripe Rule
rules.body: No thick colored border on one side of a box. Callouts use a full 1px border plus a faint tint, never Quarto's default 5px left stripe; dark-mode code blocks use a 1px Rule Grey frame, not a left stripe.

dos: **Do** use `var(--brand-*)` and `var(--hub-*)` for every color in custom CSS.
**Do** check new color pairings in both light and dark mode (text 4.5:1, icons and focus rings 3:1).
**Do** give every content page exactly one Diátaxis category so it gets its badge.
**Do** use pills for actions and labels, and 0.5rem corners for containers.
**Do** keep running text in the body column and let wide tables and code scroll inside their own box.
**Do** write screen recordings as `![alt text](file.mp4)` and give every image alt text.
**Do** check syntax-highlighting colors at 4.5:1 in both themes when changing the code themes.
donts: **Don't** hard-code palette hex values in CSS.
**Don't** add thick colored side borders (stripes) to callouts, cards, or alerts.
**Don't** set body text, buttons, or labels in Gelasio, or use Fira Code for anything but code.
**Don't** put text in IPA Field Green on a white background (about 2.9:1).
**Don't** add shadows to elements that are part of the page.
**Don't** add new fonts or load fonts from Google; the three brand fonts are self-hosted in `assets/fonts/`.
